title: Check if Linux detects a plugged-in USB drive
summary: Find out whether the system sees the USB device at all and whether the drive has a partition. This tells a hardware or cable problem apart from a mounting problem. The commands only read information and change nothing.

aliases.text: usb drive not showing up linux
usb stick plugged in but nothing happens

prerequisites: The USB drive and a USB port on the computer itself (not a hub) to try
The lsusb command comes from the usbutils package; if it is missing, install that package first

steps.explain: List the USB devices the kernel currently sees, before you plug in the drive. The first lines are usually the built-in controllers (root hubs).
steps.expect: One line per device in the form 'Bus 001 Device 002: ID 0781:5581 Vendor name'. Remember how many lines there are.

steps.explain: Plug the drive directly into a USB port on the computer, not into a hub or extension cable, and wait about 5 seconds.
List the USB devices again. A new line that names your drive's brand means the kernel detects the device, so the port, cable and drive work at this level.
steps.expect: A new line with your drive's brand or product name. If no new line appears, the cable, port or drive is the likely problem.

alternatives.explain: Show the same devices as a tree. A drive listed under a hub line is connected through that hub.

steps.explain: Check whether the drive has a disk and a partition the system can read. A disk without a partition line, or a partition without a filesystem type, cannot be mounted.
steps.expect: A disk line such as sdb with a child line such as sdb1 whose FSTYPE is vfat, exfat, ntfs or ext4. A child line with an empty FSTYPE means the filesystem is not recognized.

steps.explain: Read the latest kernel messages about USB to see errors from the moment the drive was plugged in.
steps.expect: Lines such as 'new high-speed USB device' or 'USB Mass Storage device detected' mean the kernel reacted. Repeated errors about the device descriptor point to a cable, port or power problem.

source.title: lsusb manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
